data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol is a consensus lease that treats workspace allocation as a distributed lock released only by publishing a completed evidence hash to a BFT ledger, and requires a signed absence certificate for reclamation after crash.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A view change during crash may cause the evidence hash to be accepted by a minority that is later excluded from the supermajority","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Premature lease epoch reuse may collide with in-flight evidence publications","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A temporarily reduced quorum may issue an absence certificate despite hidden evidence","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Workspace allocation writes a lease record (workspace_id, problem_digest, epoch) to a BFT ledger. The holder must periodically renew. Completion appends the evidence hash and atomically releases the lease. If the process crashes without terminal record, the lease remains active. Reclamation requires a special absence certificate signed by a supermajority of consensus participants affirming they have not accepted an evidence hash for this lease epoch. The protocol durably records the lease entry, all renewal attempts, and the signed absence certificate.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
